_note: Placements that are meant to look this way. tools\cli audit placement skips a problem whose kind matches and whose name or prefab matches the regex (docs/placement-audit.md). Give the reason a reviewer can check in a shot.

allow.why: The bag stands on the vault's own steel floor, 0.5 m above the terrain; the floor is part of the Roadmap_Bank_Vault mesh, so the trace down reads terrain (bank close-up c09, #925). It was hidden until the 'Map' in 'Roadmap_' stopped counting as a hung map.

The vault door is the prefab's own child (VaultDoor) on its hinge pivot, seated in the frame ring of VaultFront by design; in the _Open vault it stands on the same hinge beside the frame (tools/assets/bank-vault, #925). The town vault swings it open with the breach state.
The quarry axe lies flat on the ground by the logs (LoggingChain.layer angles 90).
The small money bag on the bank floor is meant to be small (#740).
The cash stack is the bag prefab's child, drawn inside the 0.4-scale bag the way the town bag is (#323 batch 0).
The annex twin of the bank bell box hangs 1.5 m up beside the twin vault door: the annex has no wall for it, and the alarm mount test only needs the box above its door (#323 batch 0).
The teller stands inside the bank on its floor (y 0.2) behind the vanilla post-office counter; the terrain probe misses the building floor (#931).

Vanilla has no cabbage-head mesh, only the whole-plant CabbageCrop_01 (0.84 x 0.91 m at scale 1). Cabbage.et scales it to 0.5, so the plant measures 0.46 m, inside the cabbage 0.15-0.6 m range. A larger scale would put a 0.9 m plant on a stall table.
A market tarp is stretched between four poles 2.4 to 2.7 m up over its stall; nothing stands under it but the stall and its trader (market-canopies).
Flag_1_2 is a plain 1 x 2 m red cloth with a white hem; scaled 2x it is a 2 x 4 m tarp, the largest flat cloth in the base game (market-canopies).
The door hood and the bulkhead light are fixed to the vault front: their backs stand in the concrete face, as wall-mounted fittings do (polish-vault-market).

The market parasol stands at the back of the registry counter and its canopy reaches over the counter top on purpose: the clerk and the counter are under cover (arrival-desk look, town-arrival-desk). The pole stands clear of the counter; only the canopy box overlaps it.
